topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section serves as the opening framing of the lecture, introducing the lecturer, topic outline, and key learning objectives.

topics.label: Intrinsic mutations, environmental exposure, and epidemiological variation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the fundamental question of whether cancer is driven primarily by intrinsic biological bad luck or environmental exposures, supported by global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Oncogenic pathogens and infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents promote malignant transformation, illustrating the concept through general pathogen mechanisms and the specific etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and oxidative cellular damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate to drive cancer progression, followed by a mechanistic summary.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity and evaluate cancer risk against practical benefits.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This section serves as the closing framing of the lecture, providing concluding remarks and summarizing the key takeaways.
